summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with acute-on-chronic epigastric abdominal pain, attributed to gastroparesis and chronic pancreatitis, along with severe hyperglycemia (glucose 615) without ketoacidosis. Pain was managed with oral hydromorphone per her narcotic contract, and insulin therapy was adjusted from 50 to 60 units of Lantus nightly due to improved oral intake and fluctuating glucose levels. She developed urinary retention likely due to narcotics and sedatives, requiring intermittent catheterization; however, she regained spontaneous voiding and did not require a Foley at discharge. A domestic violence concern was addressed, with plans for a restraining order and social support. She remained on her baseline psychiatric and gastrointestinal medications, with no major complications. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up arranged with her primary care provider and urology.
